nodes.summary: If the set of moves `A` is non-empty and `A^ℕ` carries the product of the discrete topologies, every closed payoff set `S ⊆ A^ℕ` is determined (Gale and Stewart, *Infinite games with perfect information*, Ann. of Math. Stud. 28 (1953); Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., AMS 2009, Theorem 6A.2).
nodes.title: Gale–Stewart theorem

nodes.summary: If the set of moves `A` is non-empty and `A^ℕ` carries the product of the discrete topologies, every open payoff set `S ⊆ A^ℕ` is determined (Gale and Stewart, *Infinite games with perfect information*, Ann. of Math. Stud. 28 (1953); Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., AMS 2009, Theorem 6A.2 and 6A.4).
nodes.title: Gale–Stewart theorem, open case

nodes.summary: If `A` has exactly one element, there is a single play, and every payoff set is determined: player I wins if it contains that play and player II wins otherwise. This degenerate case shows why the existence of non-determined sets needs at least two moves.
nodes.title: Games with a single move are determined

nodes.summary: The game with payoff `S ⊆ A^ℕ` is determined if one of the two players has a winning strategy (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A). If `A` is empty there are no strategies at all, so no set is determined.
nodes.title: Determined game

nodes.summary: In `σ * τ` player I follows `σ` (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: The play of two strategies follows the first one

nodes.summary: The play `x` follows `σ` at every even turn: `x 0 = σ []`, `x 2 = σ [x 0, x 1]`, … (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: Player I follows a strategy

nodes.summary: In `σ * τ` player II follows `τ` (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: The play of two strategies follows the second one

nodes.summary: The play `x` follows `τ` at every odd turn: `x 1 = τ [x 0]`, `x 3 = τ [x 0, x 1, x 2]`, … (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: Player II follows a strategy

nodes.summary: The play `x` follows the strategy `σ : List A → A` at the turns `n` with `n % 2 = k`: there `x n = σ (history x n)`. With `k = 0` these are the turns of player I and with `k = 1` those of player II (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: Following a strategy at the turns of one parity

nodes.summary: The list `[x 0, …, x (n - 1)]` of the first `n` moves of the play `x : ℕ → A`: the position the player to move at time `n` sees in a game of perfect information (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: History of a play

nodes.summary: Player II has a winning strategy in the game with payoff `S ⊆ A^ℕ`: a strategy `τ` such that every play following `τ` at player II's turns lies outside `S` (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: Player II wins a game

nodes.summary: Player I has a winning strategy in the game with payoff `S ⊆ A^ℕ`: a strategy `σ` such that every play following `σ` at player I's turns lies in `S` (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: Player I wins a game

nodes.summary: No payoff set is won by both players: the play of the two winning strategies would lie both in `S` and outside it (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: At most one player wins

nodes.summary: The unique play `σ * τ` in which player I follows `σ` and player II follows `τ`: `x n = σ (history x n)` for even `n` and `x n = τ (history x n)` for odd `n` (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., §6A).
nodes.title: The play of two strategies

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
